data.name: Sprocket.Term.LogicSystem
data.value: A ![](mark:logic-system) **logic system** is the automation for one machine, like an airlock, with all the jobs that go with running it.
data.comment: Codex page on "Logic system", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Installation
data.value: An ![](mark:installation) **installation** is a set of blocks and signals a logic system works on, like one airlock among several.
data.comment: Codex page on "Installation", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.InstallationPanel
data.value: The **installation panel** is where you set up an ![](mark:installation) [installation](Term.Installation), selecting the blocks and signals for each of its [slots](Term.Slot). Open it from the installation's row on the home screen. The logic system's `Installation panel` tab is where you choose what every panel shows.
data.comment: Codex page on "Installation panel", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Category
data.value: A **category** is a heading on the [installation panel](Term.InstallationPanel) that groups the [slots](Term.Slot) dragged under it.
data.comment: Codex page on "Category", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Slot
data.value: A **slot** is a named place in a logic system, like the inner door, that each installation fills with its own blocks or signal. A required slot that is empty, or whose blocks were lost, is filled again on the [installation panel](Term.InstallationPanel).
data.comment: Codex page on "Slot", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.LogicSystemStates
data.value: The **logic system's states** are values it remembers between runs, each installation its own, like which side of the airlock its engineer is on. Each state is on or off, or one choice of a [state type](Term.Type).
data.comment: Codex page on "Logic system states", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Type
data.value: A **state type** is a named list of choices, like *inside* and *outside*. A [state](Term.LogicSystemStates) of that state type has one of its choices.
data.comment: Codex page on "State type", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Undo
data.value: ![](mark:undo) **Undo** takes back the last change, and ![](mark:redo) **redo** makes it again. Each logic system has its own history of changes, across all its screens, and the home screen has its own.
data.comment: Codex page on "Undo", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Sequence
data.value: A ![](mark:sequence) **sequence** is a list of [steps](Term.Step) a logic system runs from top to bottom. An installation runs it once at a time, so a ![](mark:trigger) [trigger](Term.Trigger) that fires while it is running is missed.
data.comment: Codex page on "Sequence", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Step
data.value: A **step** is one line of a ![](mark:sequence) [sequence](Term.Sequence). Press one of its parts to change it in a [selector](Term.Selector) or a menu.
data.comment: Codex page on "Step", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Action
data.value: An ![](mark:action) **action** is something a block can do, like opening a door or extending a piston.
data.comment: Codex page on "Action", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Task
data.value: A **task** is one operation: running or stopping a ![](mark:sequence) [sequence](Term.Sequence), an ![](mark:action) [action](Term.Action) on blocks, or setting one of their ![](mark:value) [values](Term.Value).
data.comment: Codex page on "Task", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Value
data.value: A ![](mark:value) **value** is a block's property, like a light's color, which steps can set or check.
data.comment: Codex page on "Value", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Awaitable
data.value: An ![](mark:awaited) **awaitable** is an ![](mark:action) [action](Term.Action) that keeps working for several [ticks](Term.Tick), like a door closing, and that a ![](mark:sequence) [sequence](Term.Sequence) can wait for. Most actions are done at once, and of those that keep working, only the awaitables can be waited for.
data.comment: Codex page on "Awaitable", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Delay
data.value: A **delay** is a step that pauses its sequence for a set time, in seconds or [ticks](Term.Tick), like giving a sound time to play to its end.
data.comment: Codex page on "Delay", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.If
data.value: An **if**, also known as a *conditional*, is a step that checks blocks, or one of the logic system's [states](Term.LogicSystemStates), and runs the steps under it only when its condition passes.
data.comment: Codex page on "If", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Branch
data.value: A **branch** adds more steps to an [if](Term.If), run when the conditions above it fail. An `otherwise if` checks a condition of its own, and an `otherwise` runs when none above passed.
data.comment: Codex page on "Branch", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one. "otherwise if" and "otherwise" are the words of the branches on the screen, which stay English.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.RunAndStop
data.value: **Run** and **stop** are steps that start or stop another sequence of the same logic system, in the same installation. A sequence that is already running isn't started a second time.
data.comment: Codex page on "Run and stop", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Tick
data.value: A **tick** is the smallest step of time, sixty to a second.
data.comment: Codex page on "Tick", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Selector
data.value: A **selector** is the screen where you select what a step, an if or a trigger works with, like its blocks and what to do with them.
data.comment: Codex page on "Selector", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Trigger
data.value: A ![](mark:trigger) **trigger** runs or stops a sequence when something happens, like a button being pressed. It fires only while its logic system and installation are switched on.
data.comment: Codex page on "Trigger", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Signal
data.value: A ![](mark:signal) **signal** is what a block sends to fire a trigger, from a slot on its toolbar or from a change in the block itself.
data.comment: Codex page on "Signal", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Library
data.value: The **library** contains your ![](mark:blueprint) [blueprints](Term.Blueprint), along with the logic systems on this [construct](Term.Construct) and [backups](Term.Backup) of constructs that lost their automation.
data.comment: Codex page on "Library", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Backup
data.value: When a [construct](Term.Construct) loses its last programmable block, each of its logic systems with no ![](mark:blueprint) [blueprint](Term.Blueprint) in the library is saved there as a **backup**. Select it in the library and press `Add to this construct` to have it back.
data.comment: Codex page on "Backup", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Blueprint
data.value: A ![](mark:blueprint) **blueprint** is a copy of a logic system kept in the [library](Term.Library), ready to put on another construct. It has no blocks of its own: each construct fills its [slots](Term.Slot) with its own blocks.
data.comment: Codex page on "Blueprint", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Term.Construct
data.value: A **construct** is a grid and everything pistons, rotors and hinges attach to it. A ship docked to a station by a connector or landing gear is a construct of its own: it isn't part of the station, and its blocks can't fill the station's [slots](Term.Slot).
data.comment: Codex page on "Construct", shown in a tip. It says what the term is, naming it in bold with its mark where it has one.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Back
data.value: Back
data.comment: Tooltip on the back arrow at the left end of the editor's heading bar, shown on every screen except the home screen. Pressing it returns to the screen before.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Close
data.value: Close the editor
data.comment: Tooltip on the close cross at the far right of the editor's heading bar, shown only on the home screen, where there is no screen to go back to. Pressing it closes the editor.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Tips
data.value: Show fewer tips.
data.comment: Tooltip on the question mark in the editor's heading bar, shown while tips are on. Pressing it turns tips off, and the look of terms with them, in every world this player plays; the tips that stay are those on buttons that show only a mark and those saying why something cannot be pressed.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.TipsOn
data.value: Show every tip.
data.comment: Tooltip on the question mark in the editor's heading bar, shown while tips are off. Pressing it turns every tip back on, in every world this player plays.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Undo
data.value:
![](mark:undo) [Undo](Term.Undo)
{action}
data.comment: Tooltip on the undo arrow in the editor's heading bar, shown while there is a change to undo. {action} is one of the Sprocket.Change texts, filled in, such as Deleted step 3 in Cycle, "open Outer Door", and stands on its own line after the word Undo, or by Sprocket.Undo.Also holding that text where the undo takes changes on other screens along.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.Redo
data.value:
![](mark:redo) [Redo](Term.Undo)
{action}
data.comment: Tooltip on the redo arrow in the editor's heading bar, shown while there is an undone change to make again. {action} is one of the Sprocket.Change texts, filled in, such as Deleted step 3 in Cycle, "open Outer Door", and stands on its own line after the word Redo, or by Sprocket.Undo.Also holding that text where the redo makes changes on other screens again with it.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.Broken
data.value: Something in it needs fixing. Open it to see what.
data.comment: Tooltip on the round light at the start of a row in a list (a logic system, installation or sequence on the home screen or a logic system's screen) while the light is red because something in what the row opens needs mending.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.Ran
data.value: It ran just now.
data.comment: Tooltip on the round light at the start of a row in a list (a logic system, installation or sequence on the home screen or a logic system's screen) while the light flashes green just after the thing ran.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.Idle
data.value: It is idle. Lights green when it runs, and red when something is broken.
data.comment: Tooltip on the round light at the start of a row in a list (a logic system, installation or sequence on the home screen or a logic system's screen) while the light is dark: nothing ran a moment ago and nothing is broken.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchOn
data.value: Switch this installation on
data.comment: Tooltip on an installation's on/off switch while the switch is off, on the installation's row on the home screen and in the heading bar of the installation panel. Shown only while the installation's logic system is switched on.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchOff
data.value: Switch this installation off and stop any running sequences.
data.comment: Tooltip on an installation's on/off switch while the switch is on, on the installation's row on the home screen and in the heading bar of the installation panel. Shown only while the installation's logic system is switched on.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchSystemOn
data.value: Switch this logic system on, locking it against changes.
data.comment: Tooltip on the on/off switch of a logic system that has no installations, while it is off: on its row on the home screen and in the editor's heading bar on its screen and its sequences' screens.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchSystemOff
data.value: Switch this logic system off, stopping its sequences and unlocking it for changes.
data.comment: Tooltip on the on/off switch of a logic system that has no installations, while it is on: on its row on the home screen and in the editor's heading bar on its screen and its sequences' screens.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchBlueprintOn
data.value: Switch on every installation of this logic system
data.comment: Tooltip on the on/off switch of a logic system that has installations, while it is off: on its row on the home screen and in the editor's heading bar on its screen and its sequences' screens. Each installation then runs where its own switch is on.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchBlueprintFirst
data.value: The logic system must be switched on first.
data.comment: Tooltip on an installation's on/off switch while its logic system is switched off and the installation's switch is dimmed and cannot be pressed: on the installation's row on the home screen and in the heading bar of the installation panel.

data.name: Sprocket.Row.SwitchBlueprintOff
data.value: Switch off every installation of this logic system
data.comment: Tooltip on the on/off switch of a logic system that has installations, while it is on: on its row on the home screen and in the editor's heading bar on its screen and its sequences' screens.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.NameAbout
data.value: The name of this [construct](Term.Construct), taken from its largest grid. Renaming it renames that grid.
data.comment: Tooltip on the construct's name in the home screen's heading: the name of its largest grid, the one with the most blocks. Pressing the name renames that grid.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.NewAbout
data.value: Start a new logic system on this [construct](Term.Construct).
data.comment: Tooltip on the home screen's button that adds a new logic system to the construct.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.OpenInstanceAbout
data.value: Open the [installation panel](Term.InstallationPanel) for **{name}**.
data.comment: Tooltip on an installation's row on the home screen, under its logic system; pressing the row opens that installation's installation panel. {name} is filled with the installation's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.MakeBlueprintAbout
data.value: Keep a copy of this logic system in the library as a ![](mark:blueprint) [blueprint](Term.Blueprint).
data.comment: Tooltip on the button that makes a blueprint of a logic system, on its heading row on the home screen, and in the library on the right-pointing arrow in the strip between its panes, shown while the library holds no blueprint of the chosen logic system or backup.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.ChooseVersionAbout
data.value: Two [constructs](Term.Construct) joined, each with its own version of {name}. Both stay switched off until you select one.
data.comment: Tooltip on the Choose a version button on a logic system's heading row on the home screen. {name} is the logic system's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.UpdateFromLibraryAbout
data.value: The ![](mark:blueprint) [blueprint](Term.Blueprint) in the library has more recent changes. Update the logic system on this construct.
data.comment: Tooltip on the button on a logic system's heading row on the home screen, and in the library on the left-pointing arrow in the strip between its panes, that puts the library's newer blueprint in the logic system's place; shown where the blueprint was changed after the logic system.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.UpdateBlueprintAbout
data.value: Update the ![](mark:blueprint) [blueprint](Term.Blueprint) from this construct's logic system.
data.comment: Tooltip on the button on a logic system's heading row on the home screen, and in the library on the right-pointing arrow in the strip between its panes, that brings the library's blueprint up to date from the logic system; shown once the library holds a blueprint and the logic system was changed after it.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.EditBlueprint
data.value: Opens the **{name}** logic system editor.
data.comment: Tooltip on a logic system's heading row on the home screen, and on the logic system's name in the editor's heading bar on the installation panel; pressing either opens the logic system's screen. {name} is filled with the logic system's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.AddAnotherAbout
data.value: Install the **{name}** logic system on another set of blocks.
data.comment: Tooltip on the home screen's button under a logic system's installations that adds another installation. {name} is filled with the logic system's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.OpenAbout
data.value: Name this [slot](Term.Slot) and say what it is for.
data.comment: Tooltip on a slot's name in the slots list on a logic system's screen, while the logic system can be changed. Pressing the name opens the slot's page, where it is named and described.

data.name: Sprocket.System.NameAbout
data.value: This logic system's name.
data.comment: Tooltip on a logic system's name in the editor's heading bar on its own screen, where pressing the name renames the logic system.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Delete
data.value: Delete this logic system, and every installation of it
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin in the editor's heading bar on a logic system's screen, which deletes the logic system together with every installation of it.

data.name: Sprocket.System.DeleteInstallation
data.value: Delete this installation
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin of an installation's row on the home screen, which deletes that installation.

data.name: Sprocket.System.UsingAbout
data.value: Select the ![](mark:installation) [installation](Term.Installation) whose blocks this screen shows. Blocks you select for a step or a trigger fill its [slots](Term.Slot).
data.comment: Tooltip on the list of a logic system's installations at the top of its screen; the installation picked there fills the slots named in the screen's sentences.

data.name: Sprocket.System.TabFlagged
data.value: Something on this tab needs attention. The row with the problem says what.
data.comment: Tooltip on the warning mark beside the name of a logic system's Triggers tab or Sequences tab, shown while something on that tab has a problem (red) or a warning (amber); the row it concerns says what is wrong.

data.name: Sprocket.System.WhenAbout
data.value: Perform a [task](Term.Task) when a block sends a ![](mark:signal) [signal](Term.Signal) or reaches a requested state.
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice in the add-trigger menu on a logic system's screen that adds a trigger started by a block's signal or state.

data.name: Sprocket.System.EveryAbout
data.value: Repeat a [task](Term.Task) at a set interval.
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice in the add-trigger menu on a logic system's screen that adds a trigger started on a timer.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.StateAbout
data.value: Select another state, or another value for it.
data.comment: Tooltip on the part of a trigger's sentence, on a logic system's screen, that names one of the logic system's states; pressing it opens the picker the trigger was made with.

data.name: Sprocket.System.Copy
data.value: Copy this sequence. The copy starts switched off and without ![](mark:trigger) [triggers](Term.Trigger).
data.comment: Tooltip on the copy mark of a sequence's row on a logic system's screen, for a sequence that a trigger starts.

data.name: Sprocket.System.CopyUnstarted
data.value: Copy this sequence. The copy starts switched off.
data.comment: Tooltip on the copy mark of a sequence's row on a logic system's screen, for a sequence that no trigger starts.

data.name: Sprocket.System.OpenSequence
data.value: Open **{name}** to see and change its steps.
data.comment: Tooltip on a sequence's row on a logic system's screen; pressing the row opens the sequence's screen. {name} is filled with the sequence's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.Delete
data.value: Delete this trigger
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin at the end of a trigger's row on a logic system's screen, while the trigger can be deleted.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.Copy
data.value: Duplicate this trigger.
data.comment: Tooltip on the copy mark near the end of a trigger's row on a logic system's screen, while the trigger can be copied.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.BlocksAbout
data.value: Select the block that fires this trigger.
data.comment: Tooltip on the part of a trigger's sentence, on a logic system's screen, that names the block that starts it. Pressing the part changes the block.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.DoesAbout
data.value: Select what this trigger does.
data.comment: Tooltip on the part of a trigger's sentence, on a logic system's screen, that names the sequence it starts or the action it does. Pressing the part changes it.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.RateAbout
data.value: Change how often it should run.
data.comment: Tooltip on the length in an Every trigger's sentence on a logic system's screen, which says how often the trigger runs. Pressing it opens the length panel.

data.name: Sprocket.Trigger.TargetsAbout
data.value: Select which blocks this trigger acts on.
data.comment: Tooltip on the part of a trigger's sentence, on a logic system's screen, that names the blocks the trigger's own action acts on. Pressing the part changes them.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.NameAbout
data.value: This sequence's name.
data.comment: Tooltip on a sequence's name in the editor's heading bar on its own screen, where pressing the name renames the sequence.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DoSomethingAbout
data.value: Perform an ![](mark:action) [action](Term.Action) on blocks or set one of their ![](mark:value) [values](Term.Value).
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice in the add-step menu on a sequence's screen that adds a task: an action on blocks, or setting one of their values.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.Delete
data.value: Delete this sequence
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin of a sequence's row on a logic system's screen, and on the bin in the editor's heading bar on a sequence's screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DeleteStep
data.value: Delete this step
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin at the end of a step's row on a sequence's screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.CopyStep
data.value: Duplicate this step.
data.comment: Tooltip on the copy mark of a step's row on a sequence's screen. An if is copied with the steps in it.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.ActionAbout
data.value: Select what this step does.
data.comment: Tooltip on the action named in a step's sentence on a sequence's screen; pressing it opens the picker to choose what the step does.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.BlocksAbout
data.value: Select which blocks this step acts on.
data.comment: Tooltip on the blocks named in a step's sentence on a sequence's screen; pressing them opens the picker to choose which blocks the step acts on.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.OptionsAbout
data.value: Change the action's options.
data.comment: Tooltip on the options of an action, such as a piston's position and speed, in a step's sentence on a sequence's screen and in a trigger's sentence on a logic system's screen; pressing them opens the picker on the action's options.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.NewValueAbout
data.value: Change the value to set.
data.comment: Tooltip on the new value in the sentence of a step or trigger that sets a value of blocks, on a sequence's screen and on a logic system's screen; pressing it opens the picker on that value.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.ComparedAbout
data.value: Choose how it is compared.
data.comment: Tooltip on the comparison in an if's sentence on a sequence's screen, such as "is" or "is below"; pressing it opens a menu of the comparisons the value can be checked with.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.ReadAbout
data.value: Choose whether any or all of the blocks must pass, or whether their sum or average is checked.
data.comment: Tooltip on how an if reads its blocks where it names several: on the part of its sentence on a sequence's screen, and on the box over the column of blocks in the selector an if or a trigger on a number is made with. The choices are "any", "all / each", "the sum of" and "the average of"; the sentence says "all" as "each" where it reads a value, and pressing either opens a menu of them.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.CheckedAbout
data.value: Change the value to check for.
data.comment: Tooltip on the value an if checks blocks for, in the if's sentence on a sequence's screen; pressing it opens the picker on that value.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.ReadWithAbout
data.value: Change what the value is read with.
data.comment: Tooltip on what a value is read with, such as the button whose label it reads, straight after the value in the sentence of an if on a sequence's screen or of a trigger on a logic system's screen; pressing it opens the picker on it.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.LengthAbout
data.value: Change how long the delay is.
data.comment: Tooltip on a wait step's length in its sentence on a sequence's screen; pressing it opens the panel where the length is given.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.DragStep
data.value: Drag to move this step.
data.comment: Tooltip on the drag handle of a step's row on a sequence's screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.PauseStep
data.value: Pause this step. The sequence skips it until it is resumed.
data.comment: Tooltip on the pause mark of a step's row on a sequence's screen, while the step is not paused; pressing it pauses the step.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.UnpauseStep
data.value: Paused: the sequence skips this step. Press to resume it.
data.comment: Tooltip on the pause mark of a step's row on a sequence's screen, lit while the step is paused; pressing it resumes the step.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.WaitTypedAbout
data.value: 60 ticks is one second.
data.comment: Tooltip on the number box where a length of time is typed: in the panel for a wait's length on a sequence's screen, the panel for a timer trigger's interval on a logic system's screen, and the column choosing how often a new timer trigger fires.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.RunsAbout
data.value: Select which sequence this step runs.
data.comment: Tooltip on the sequence a run step names, on a sequence's screen, such as Cycle Out in "run Cycle Out". Pressing it opens the list of sequences to choose another.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.StopsAbout
data.value: Select which sequence this step stops.
data.comment: Tooltip on the sequence a stop step names, on a sequence's screen, such as Cycle Out in "stop Cycle Out". Pressing it opens the list of sequences to choose another.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.WatchedAbout
data.value: Select which ![](mark:value) [value](Term.Value) this trigger watches.
data.comment: Tooltip on the value a trigger on a number watches, on a logic system's screen, such as power in "when any power of Battery < 20". Pressing it opens the trigger's picker on the value.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.FillsAbout
data.value: Select what fills this [slot](Term.Slot).
data.comment: Tooltip on a slot's blocks, and on the signal beside them, on an installation panel. Pressing either opens the picker the slot is filled with.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.StepBlocks
data.value: Blocks this step acts on:
data.comment: First line of the tooltip on the blocks of a step or an if on a sequence's screen, once it holds blocks, under the slot they come from; a list of them follows.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.TriggerBlocks
data.value: Blocks that fire this trigger:
data.comment: First line of the tooltip on the blocks a trigger watches, on a logic system's screen, once it holds blocks, under the slot they come from; a list of them follows.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.TriggerTargets
data.value: Blocks this trigger acts on:
data.comment: First line of the tooltip on the blocks a trigger's own action acts on, on a logic system's screen, once it holds blocks, under the slot they come from; a list of them follows.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.FromSlot
data.value: From the slot {slots}.
data.comment: In the tooltip on the blocks of a step or a trigger, above the line that heads the list of the blocks: the slot of the logic system the blocks fill. {slots} is the slot's name, in bold.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.SlotEmpty
data.value: It is empty in this installation.
data.comment: In the tooltip on the slot a step or a trigger names, under the line naming the slot, where the installation shown has no block in it.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.FromSlots
data.value: From the slots {slots}.
data.comment: In the tooltip on the blocks of a step or a trigger, above the line that heads the list of the blocks, where they come from more than one slot. {slots} is the slots' names, in bold, separated by commas.

data.name: Sprocket.Part.ScreenOf
data.value: {block}: {screen}
data.comment: One line of the list in the tooltip on a slot of screens a step or a trigger names, on a sequence's screen and a logic system's screen: a block the installation shown fills the slot with, and the screen of it the slot holds. {block} is the block's name, {screen} the screen's name as the block calls it, such as Front.

data.name: Sprocket.Chrome.DoneAbout
data.value: Keep any changes and return.
data.comment: Tooltip on the Done button in the editor's heading bar on a logic system's screen, a sequence's screen, the installation panel and a blueprint slot's screen, where every change is kept as soon as it is made.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.DoneFirst
data.value: Select something in every column first.
data.comment: Tooltip on the Done button in the editor's heading bar in the picker, and on the page choosing how often a timer trigger fires, while it cannot be pressed yet.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Back
data.value: Back
data.comment: Tooltip on the narrow folded column at the left edge of the picker, which turns back to the picker's page before.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.Next
data.value: Next
data.comment: Tooltip on the narrow folded column at the right edge of the picker, which turns on to the picker's page after.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.ClearTyped
data.value: Clear what is typed
data.comment: Tooltip on the cross at the end of a search box in the picker, which empties the box.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.EveryKind
data.value: Show every kind again
data.comment: Tooltip on the cross beside the kind of block that the picker's column of blocks is narrowed to; pressing it shows every kind again.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.ShowHidden
data.value: Show blocks hidden from toolbars
data.comment: Tooltip on the closed eye at the end of the heading of the picker's column of blocks; pressing it also lists the blocks set not to show in the toolbar config.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.HideHidden
data.value: Hide blocks hidden from toolbars
data.comment: Tooltip on the open eye at the end of the heading of the picker's column of blocks; pressing it takes the blocks set not to show in the toolbar config out of the list again.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.KindAbout
data.value: Show only one kind of block.
data.comment: Tooltip on the line in the picker's column of blocks that opens the list of kinds of block.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SourceAbout
data.value: Select what this step, if or trigger works with. `Existing slot` uses a [slot](Term.Slot) the logic system has already.
data.comment: Tooltip on the Source box heading the first column of the selector a step, an if, an otherwise if or a when is made with, which chooses what it works with: blocks, a slot the logic system already has (the choice Existing slot, quoted here as the box shows it), or, for all but a step, one of the logic system's states.

data.name: Sprocket.Member.Waits
data.value: This is ![](mark:awaited) [awaitable](Term.Awaitable). The sequence goes straight on while it works, and a `wait for pending tasks` step below waits for it to finish.
data.comment: Tooltip on an awaitable action, one marked with the clock that works over several ticks: on its row in the selector and on its part of a sentence. Also the tooltip on a step's sentence on a sequence's screen when the step starts such an action and goes straight on. "wait for pending tasks" is the words of the step that waits, which stay English.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.RunAbout
data.value: Start the sequence selected below
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice at the top of the picker's column choosing what a trigger does that makes the trigger start the sequence chosen in that column.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.StopAbout
data.value: Stop the sequence selected below
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice at the top of the picker's column choosing what a trigger does that makes the trigger stop the sequence chosen in that column.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.StateFixedValueAbout
data.value: Use one of these values.
data.comment: Said where the pointer rests on the label before the buttons for the state's own values, in the selector that sets, tests or watches one of the logic system's states.

data.name: Sprocket.State.TypeRenameAbout
data.value: Rename this state type
data.comment: Tooltip on a state type's name on a logic system's State tab, with its pencil. Pressing it lets the name be typed.

data.name: Sprocket.State.ChoiceAbout
data.value: Rename or remove this choice
data.comment: Tooltip on one of a state type's choices on a logic system's State tab. Pressing it opens a menu offering to rename or remove it.

data.name: Sprocket.State.StateRenameAbout
data.value: Rename this state
data.comment: Tooltip on a state's name on a logic system's State tab, with its pencil. Pressing it lets the name be typed.

data.name: Sprocket.State.TypeRemove
data.value: Remove this state type
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin beside a state type on a logic system's State tab.

data.name: Sprocket.State.TypeKept
data.value: A state uses this state type, so it cannot be removed.
data.comment: Tooltip on the dimmed bin beside a state type on a logic system's State tab, where a state holds one of its choices.

data.name: Sprocket.State.StateRemove
data.value: Remove this state
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin beside a state on a logic system's State tab.

data.name: Sprocket.State.StateKept
data.value: A step or trigger uses this state, so it cannot be removed.
data.comment: Tooltip on the dimmed bin beside a state on a logic system's State tab, where a step sets it or something tests or watches it.

data.name: Sprocket.State.TypeDrag
data.value: Drag to move the state type.
data.comment: Tooltip on the grip beside a state type on a logic system's State tab.

data.name: Sprocket.State.StateDrag
data.value: Drag to move the state.
data.comment: Tooltip on the grip beside a state on a logic system's State tab.

data.name: Sprocket.State.HoldsAbout
data.value: Change this state's type. Its starting value becomes the first value of the new type.
data.comment: Said where the pointer rests on what a state holds, after its name on a logic system's State tab.

data.name: Sprocket.State.StartsAbout
data.value: The value the state has when the logic system starts.
data.comment: Said where the pointer rests on the words before a state's starting value, on the State tab and in the picker that sets, tests or watches a state.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.StateNameAbout
data.value: Every slot, state type and state in a logic system needs its own name.
data.comment: Said where the pointer rests on the name of a new state in the picker that sets, tests or watches a state.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.StateTypeAbout
data.value: The [state type](Term.Type) decides which values the new state can have.
data.comment: Said where the pointer rests on the state type of a new state in the picker that sets, tests or watches a state.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.TypeNameAbout
data.value: Every slot, state type and state in a logic system needs its own name.
data.comment: Said where the pointer rests on the name of a new state type in the picker that sets, tests or watches a state.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.StateValueOfAbout
data.value: Use whatever value another state has when this runs.
data.comment: Said where the pointer rests on the other states whose value can be taken, in the picker that sets, tests or watches a state.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SlotMatched
data.value: This uses [slots](Term.Slot) the logic system has already. Rename them on its `Installation panel` tab.
data.comment: Tooltip on the picker's heading while it shows, in italics, the names of slots the logic system already has: either the blocks picked fill them exactly, or they were picked by name with the Existing slot source. These names cannot be changed here.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SlotChanges
data.value: The blocks selected replace this [slot](Term.Slot)'s blocks in the installation shown. Its name stays the same.
data.comment: Tooltip on the picker's heading while it shows the name of the slot a step or a trigger names, which the blocks picked will change because no slot holds them already. Where other steps or triggers use the slot too, Done asks whether to change it for all of them.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.SlotNameAbout
data.value: The blocks selected make a new [slot](Term.Slot) with this name. Press the name to change it.
data.comment: Tooltip on the picker's heading while it shows the name of the slot the blocks picked will make, which no slot the logic system has fills exactly. Pressing it renames the slot before it is made; the name starts as the next numbered slot name.

data.name: Sprocket.Pick.LimitAbout
data.value: This slot takes {kind} blocks.
data.comment: Tooltip on the top entry of the list of kinds of block in the picker's column of blocks, while the picker fills a slot of one kind on the installation panel; the entry stands where Anything stands otherwise. {kind} is the name of the kind the slot takes, such as Piston.

data.name: Sprocket.State.KindKept
data.value: A step, if or trigger uses this state, so its type cannot be changed.
data.comment: Said where the pointer rests on what a state holds, on its row on a logic system's State tab, while a step or a trigger uses the state, so its state type cannot be changed.

data.name: Sprocket.State.NowAbout
data.value: The value this state has right now in the installation shown.
data.comment: Tooltip on what the installation shown holds in a state, on its row on a logic system's State tab.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.NameAbout
data.value: This installation's name.
data.comment: Tooltip on the installation's name in the editor's heading bar on the installation panel. Pressing the name renames the installation.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.NameBoxAbout
data.value: The slot's name, as everyone filling in this logic system sees it.
data.comment: Tooltip on the slot's name in the editor's heading bar on a slot's page. Pressing the name renames the slot.

data.name: Sprocket.Blueprint.RequiredAbout
data.value: Set whether an installation of this logic system may leave this slot empty.
data.comment: Tooltip on the required/optional switch on a slot's page.

data.name: Sprocket.Writing.OpenAbout
data.value: Write the whole text on a page of its own.
data.comment: Tooltip on the Edit button at the right end of a step's field for text written over several lines.

data.name: Sprocket.Writing.PreviewAbout
data.value: Show the text as others will see it.
data.comment: The tooltip on the button by the description box on a logic system's screen and on a slot's screen that shows the text as it will read.

data.name: Sprocket.Color.Hue
data.value: Hue
data.comment: Tooltip on the H slider of the color picker in the picker's values column.

data.name: Sprocket.Color.Saturation
data.value: Saturation
data.comment: Tooltip on the S slider of the color picker in the picker's values column.

data.name: Sprocket.Color.Brightness
data.value: Brightness
data.comment: Tooltip on the V slider of the color picker in the picker's values column.

data.name: Sprocket.Color.PlaneAbout
data.value: Saturation across, brightness up.
data.comment: Tooltip on the square of the color picker where saturation and brightness are chosen together.

data.name: Sprocket.Color.CodeAbout
data.value: Enter a color as #RRGGBB, or #RRGGBBAA to include its opacity.
data.comment: Tooltip on the box under the sliders of the color picker, in the picker's values column, where a color code is typed.

data.name: Sprocket.System.TurnOffToEdit
data.value: The system must be turned off in order to make changes safely.
data.comment: Tooltip on a part or button that cannot be pressed while its logic system is switched on: the copy marks and bins of trigger and sequence rows and the slot rows on a logic system's screen, and the parts of steps on a sequence's screen.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.RunNow
data.value: Run this sequence manually now
data.comment: Tooltip on the play button in the editor's heading bar on a sequence's screen, and on the play button of each sequence's row on a logic system's screen, while the sequence is not running; pressing it runs the sequence by hand.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.StopNow
data.value: Stop this sequence where it is
data.comment: Tooltip on the stop button in the editor's heading bar on a sequence's screen, and on the stop button of each sequence's row on a logic system's screen, while the sequence is running; pressing it stops the sequence and leaves every block as it is.

data.name: Sprocket.Withheld.Events
data.value: *The game keeps this block's events from mods. Set this in the terminal.*
data.comment: Tooltip on a dimmed member in the picker that cannot be chosen, because the game keeps this block's events from mods.

data.name: Sprocket.Withheld.Camera
data.value: *Choosing a camera here is not available yet. Set it in the terminal.*
data.comment: Tooltip on a dimmed member in the selector, one that chooses a camera, which the automation cannot choose yet; it is set in the block's terminal.

data.name: Sprocket.Withheld.Rotor
data.value: *Choosing a rotor here is not available yet. Set it in the terminal.*
data.comment: Tooltip on a dimmed member in the selector, one that chooses a rotor, which the automation cannot choose yet; it is set in the block's terminal.

data.name: Sprocket.Withheld.Ammo
data.value: *Choosing ammunition here is not available yet. Set it in the terminal.*
data.comment: Tooltip on a dimmed member in the selector, one that chooses ammunition, which the automation cannot choose yet; it is set in the block's terminal.

data.name: Sprocket.Withheld.Unread
data.value: *The game doesn't let mods read this value's choices. Set it in the terminal.*
data.comment: Tooltip on a dimmed member in the picker that cannot be chosen yet, because its values cannot be read yet.

data.name: Sprocket.Wait.Shorter
data.value: Shorter
data.comment: In the length panel (opened by pressing a wait step's length on a sequence's screen or a timer trigger's rate on a logic system's screen, and part of the picker for a timer trigger): the tooltip on the minus button left of the number, which makes the length shorter.

data.name: Sprocket.Wait.Longer
data.value: Longer
data.comment: In the length panel (opened by pressing a wait step's length on a sequence's screen or a timer trigger's rate on a logic system's screen, and part of the picker for a timer trigger): the tooltip on the plus button right of the number, which makes the length longer.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.ShortAbout
data.value: The label shown on each button and toolbar slot that sends this signal. Left empty, they show the slot's name.
data.comment: Tooltip on the short name box on a signal slot's screen, under the Short name heading.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.ForgetBackup
data.value: Forget this backup
data.comment: In the library, the tooltip on the bin at the end of a backup's row in the section of backups.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Forget
data.value: Delete it from storage
data.comment: In the library, the tooltip on the bin at the end of a blueprint's row in the section of blueprints kept in storage.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.PutOn
data.value: Add to this construct as a logic system, with an empty installation to fill.
data.comment: In the library, the tooltip on the left-pointing arrow in the strip between its panes while a blueprint or backup is chosen: pressing it puts that one on the construct the editor was opened on as a logic system with one empty installation.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.TakeOff
data.value: Take this logic system and its installations off this construct.
data.comment: On the home screen, the tooltip on the minus in a logic system's heading row, shown where the logic system's blueprint is in the library.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Same
data.value: The blueprint in the library is the same as this logic system.
data.comment: In the library, the tooltip on the right-pointing arrow in the strip between its panes, which makes or updates a blueprint, while it cannot be pressed because the chosen logic system and its blueprint in the library are the same.

data.name: Sprocket.Systems.KeepsOne
data.value: A logic system needs at least one installation.
data.comment: Tooltip on the dimmed bin of an installation's row on the home screen, shown when it is the logic system's only installation and so cannot be deleted.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.CopyAbout
data.value: Duplicate this logic system on this construct.
data.comment: In the library, the tooltip on the copy mark in the strip between its panes: it puts a copy of the chosen logic system on this construct as a separate logic system. It can be pressed only while a logic system on this construct is chosen.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.PromoteAbout
data.value: Make this [backup](Term.Backup) a ![](mark:blueprint) [blueprint](Term.Blueprint).
data.comment: In the library, the tooltip on the right-pointing arrow in the strip between its panes while a backup is chosen: pressing it makes the backup a blueprint in storage, no longer marked as a backup.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.Deletes
data.value: Delete this logic system, with its installations. It has no blueprint in the library, so this is its only copy.
data.comment: On the home screen, the tooltip on the bin in a logic system's heading row, shown where the logic system has no blueprint in the library.

data.name: Sprocket.Library.ResetAbout
data.value: Reset this logic system to its blueprint in the library. Installations keep their blocks.
data.comment: In the library, the tooltip on the left-pointing arrow in the strip between its panes, which puts the chosen logic system's blueprint back in its place, shown while the logic system has changed since that blueprint.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.OtherwiseIfAbout
data.value: Check another condition when none above passed.
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice in the add-branch menu on the row closing an if, on a sequence's screen, that adds an otherwise if branch.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.OtherwiseAbout
data.value: Run this when none of the conditions above pass.
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice in the add-branch menu on the row closing an if, on a sequence's screen, that adds an otherwise branch.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.BranchAbout
data.value: Add a [branch](Term.Branch) to this if.
data.comment: Tooltip on the plus button on the row closing an if on a sequence's screen, which opens the menu of branches to add to the if.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.OtherwiseTestAbout
data.value: Add a condition to this branch.
data.comment: Tooltip on the button on an if's otherwise line on a sequence's screen that gives the branch something to check, which makes it an otherwise if.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.StateAbout
data.value: Select the condition that must pass.
data.comment: Tooltip on the part of an if's sentence on a sequence's screen that says what it checks of its blocks, such as "is closed"; pressing it chooses another check.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.SetStateAbout
data.value: Give one of this logic system's [states](Term.LogicSystemStates) a new value.
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice in the add-step menu on a sequence's screen that adds a step setting one of the logic system's states.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.SystemStateAbout
data.value: Select another state, or another value for it.
data.comment: Tooltip on the part of a step's sentence on a sequence's screen that names one of the logic system's states; pressing it opens the picker the step was made with.

data.name: Sprocket.Admin.EveryWorldAbout
data.value: Every world follows these settings where its own is left at `Default`. On a dedicated server they cover the worlds it hosts, and in your own game every world you play or host.
data.comment: In the admin settings, the tooltip on the tab for the defaults every world follows.

data.name: Sprocket.Admin.DefaultAbout
data.value: Use the value set under Every world, and follow it if it changes later.
data.comment: In the admin settings, the tooltip on the first choice in each setting's list on the tab for this world, the choice that follows the value set on the tab for every world. Every world in the text is that tab's name.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.AwaitAbout
data.value: Wait until every ![](mark:awaited) [awaitable](Term.Awaitable) started above has finished.
data.comment: Tooltip on the choice in the add-step menu on a sequence's screen that adds a row waiting for every awaitable action started before it. ![](mark:awaited) draws the clock mark an awaitable action carries.

data.name: Sprocket.Sequence.AwaitRow
data.value: The ![](mark:awaited) [awaitables](Term.Awaitable) started since the last `wait for pending tasks` run together, and the sequence waits here until all of them have finished.
data.comment: Tooltip on the words of a row waiting for every awaitable action started before it, on a sequence's screen. The row reads "wait for pending tasks", which stays English; ![](mark:awaited) draws the clock mark an awaitable action carries.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.RenameAbout
data.value: Rename this category
data.comment: Tooltip on a category's name, with its pencil, a heading among the slots on a logic system's Installation panel tab. Pressing it lets the name be typed.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Remove
data.value: Remove this category. Its slots stay, under no category.
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin beside a category's name, a heading among the slots on a logic system's Installation panel tab.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.OptimizeAbout
data.value: Reduce the slots to as few as the steps and triggers need.
data.comment: Tooltip on the Optimize slots button on the installation panel tab of a logic system's screen, at the right end of the SLOTS heading, while the logic system is switched off and the slots can be changed.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.RemoveAbout
data.value: Remove this unused slot.
data.comment: Tooltip on the bin beside a slot no step, if or trigger names, on the installation panel and on the Installation panel tab of a logic system's screen, while the logic system is switched off. Pressing it removes the slot, with every installation's blocks in it.

data.name: Sprocket.Category.Drag
data.value: Drag to move the category with its slots.
data.comment: Tooltip on the grip beside a category's name, a heading among the slots on a logic system's Installation panel tab.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.Drag
data.value: Drag to move the slot. At the bottom of a category, drag right to put it in or left to leave it out.
data.comment: Tooltip on the grip beside a slot's name on a logic system's Installation panel tab.

data.name: Sprocket.Slot.ExpectsAbout
data.value: The kind of block that can fill this slot. Press it to choose another.
data.comment: Tooltip on the type of block a block slot takes, under the Expects heading on the slot's page. Pressing it opens a picker listing the types the slot can take, wider or narrower, down to one kind of block; only those offering everything the slot's steps and triggers do with it.

data.name: Sprocket.Writing.MarkupAbout
data.value: Show the guide to writing rich text.
data.comment: The tooltip on the button by the description box on a logic system's screen and on a slot's screen that opens the guide to formatting text.
